From what I've seen, I think people are getting smarter in some ways, but dumber in others. I mean, we have access to so much information now, and technology is advancing at an incredible rate. Kids are learning at a younger age, and they're exposed to so many different subjects and ideas. That's amazing!

But, on the other hand, I think we're also losing some of the basics. I see a lot of kids who are really struggling with social skills, empathy, and critical thinking. They're so focused on screens and instant gratification that they're missing out on some of the fundamental skills that are essential for success.

And it's not just the kids, either. I think adults are getting dumber in some ways, too. We're so busy and stressed out that we're not taking the time to learn new things or engage in meaningful conversations. We're just going through the motions, you know?

I think it's all about balance. We need to find a way to harness the benefits of technology and modern society while still teaching kids (and adults!) the importance of social skills, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence. That's why I'm so passionate about my work in early childhood education – I want to help kids develop those skills from the get-go.
